g.title: PI
g.text: Physical pin numbers (odd = inner row from the SD-card end). One I2C bus (pins 3/5) for thermal + both ToFs; three boards share it, so chain through their second headers or a mini breadboard — one female per Pi pin. Pins 4/8/10/34 = the LD2450: 5 V on pin 4 only, never on 8 or 10.

g.title: W_MLX
g.text: to the turret: leave a service loop for tilt

g.title: W_LD2450
g.text: 5V, GND, radar TX → Pi RXD, radar RX ← Pi TXD — one 4-wire Dupont lead

g.title: MLX
g.text: On I2C-1 with the two ToFs (no address clash: 0x33 / 0x29 / 0x30). 400 kHz gives 8 fps; station.py uses 4. Rides beside the webcam on the tilt bracket.

g.title: TOF_F
g.text: VL53L1X ToF FRONT (0x29 → re-addressed 0x30 by XSHUT)

Both ToFs share I2C-1 and boot at 0x29. At every start sensing/tof.py holds BOTH XSHUT low, wakes FRONT alone and moves it to 0x30, then wakes REAR (0x29). Waking both before the change would move both.

g.title: TOF_R
g.text: XSHUT on BCM 27 so the Pi can reset it independently.

g.title: MIC
g.text: L/R tied to GND = left channel. On the post front face, 120 mm up (assembly.py).

g.title: LD2450
g.text: Silkscreen 5V GND TX RX; 5 V supply, 3.3 V UART, 256000 baud. No adapter: straight onto the Pi header — the Pi's own UART (/dev/ttyAMA0 once pi/enable_gpio_uart.sh has run). Powered OFF by default: same 24 GHz band as the LD2410Cs, interference untested.
